sanskrit: tataḥ samutpetur udāyudhās te; mahīkṣito baddhatalāṅgulitrāḥ jighāṃsamānāḥ kururājaputrāv; amarṣayanto 'rjunabhīmasenau
english: Then those kings leapt up with weapons raised, their fingers bound with finger-guards, intent on killing the two sons of the Kuru king, inflamed with rage at Arjuna and Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tatas tu bhīmo 'dbhutavīryakarmā; mahābalo vajrasamānavīryaḥ utpāṭya dorbhyāṃ drumam ekavīro; niṣpatrayām āsa yathā gajendraḥ
english: Then Bhīma, that hero of wondrous valor in battle, mighty as a thunderbolt, that lone champion, uprooted a tree with his two arms and stripped it of its branches, as a lordly elephant would do.

sanskrit: taṃ vṛkṣam ādāya ripupramāthī; daṇḍīva daṇḍaṃ pitṛrāja ugram tasthau samīpe puruṣarṣabhasya; pārthasya pārthaḥ pṛthudīrghabāhuḥ
english: Taking that tree like Yama grasping his terrible staff, the slayer of foes — that Pārtha of broad and long arms — stood close beside the bull among men, Arjuna.

sanskrit: tat prekṣya karmātimanuṣyabuddher; jiṣṇoḥ sahabhrātur acintyakarmā dāmodaro bhrātaram ugravīryaṃ; halāyudhaṃ vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe
english: Witnessing that feat which surpassed human comprehension — the deed of Jiṣṇu together with his brother — Dāmodara of inconceivable acts spoke these words to his brother of fierce valor, Halaayudha.

sanskrit: ya eṣa mattarṣabhatulyagāmī; mahad dhanuḥ karṣati tālamātram eṣo 'rjuno nātra vicāryam asti; yady asmi saṃkarṣaṇa vāsudevaḥ
english: "He who moves like a rutting bull and draws that great bow measuring a palm-tree's height — he is Arjuna; there is no doubt about this. If I am Vāsudeva, O Sankarshana."

sanskrit: ya eṣa vṛkṣaṃ tarasāvarujya; rājñāṃ vikāre sahasā nivṛttaḥ vṛkodaro nānya ihaitad adya; kartuṃ samartho bhuvi martyadharmā
english: "And he who, having swiftly uprooted that tree at the tumult of the kings, has now turned back — he is Vṛkodara; no other among mortal men on this earth would be capable of that today."

sanskrit: yo 'sau purastāt kamalāyatākṣas; tanur mahāsiṃhagatir vinītaḥ gauraḥ pralambojjvalacārughoṇo; viniḥsṛtaḥ so 'cyuta dharmarājaḥ
english: "He who stands foremost with lotus-wide eyes, slender, with the gait of a great lion, composed, fair-complexioned, with a long, gleaming and beautiful nose — he who has stepped forth, O Acyuta, is the Dharmarāja."

sanskrit: yau tau kumārāv iva kārttikeyau; dvāv aśvineyāv iti me pratarkaḥ muktā hi tasmāj jatuveśmadāhān; mayā śrutāḥ pāṇḍusutāḥ pṛthā ca
english: "Those two who appear like a pair of young Karttikeyas — they are the two sons of the Aśvins, so I surmise; for I have heard that the sons of Pāṇḍu and Pṛthā escaped from the burning of the house of lac."

sanskrit: tam abravīn nirmalatoyadābho; halāyudho 'nantarajaṃ pratītaḥ prīto 'smi diṣṭyā hi pitṛṣvasā naḥ; pṛthā vimuktā saha kauravāgryaiḥ
english: Halaayudha, radiant as pure water, glad and confident, spoke to his younger brother: "I am delighted, for by fortune our father's sister Pṛthā has been freed together with the foremost of the Kauravas."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ajināni vidhunvantaḥ karakāṃś ca dvijarṣabhāḥ ūcus taṃ bhīr na kartavyā vayaṃ yotsyāmahe parān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Shaking their antelope skins and water-pots, those foremost among twice-born ones spoke to him: "Have no fear — we shall fight the enemies."

sanskrit: tān evaṃ vadato viprān arjunaḥ prahasann iva uvāca prekṣakā bhūtvā yūyaṃ tiṣṭhata pārśvataḥ
english: Arjuna, as if smiling, spoke to those brahmins who were saying this: "You stand to the side as spectators."

sanskrit: aham enān ajihmāgraiḥ śataśo vikirañ śaraiḥ vārayiṣyāmi saṃkruddhān mantrair āśīviṣān iva
english: "I shall hold back these enraged ones by scattering hundreds of straight-tipped arrows upon them, as mantras hold back venomous serpents."

sanskrit: iti tad dhanur ādāya śulkāvāptaṃ mahārathaḥ bhrātrā bhīmena sahitas tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Having said this, that great warrior took up the bow won as the bride-price and stood together with his brother Bhīma, immovable as a mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇamukhān kruddhān kṣatriyāṃs tān ruṣotthitān saṃpetatur abhītau tau gajau pratigajān iva
english: Then those two fearless ones charged against those angry kshatriyas led by Karṇa who had risen up in fury, as two bull-elephants charge against rival elephants.

sanskrit: ūcuś ca vācaḥ paruṣās te rājāno jighāṃsavaḥ āhave hi dvijasyāpi vadho dṛṣṭo yuyutsataḥ
english: And those kings, intent on killing, spoke harsh words: "Even the slaying of a twice-born man in battle is justified when he desires to fight."

sanskrit: tato vaikartanaḥ karṇo jagāmārjunam ojasā yuddhārthī vāśitāhetor gajaḥ pratigajaṃ yathā
english: Then Karṇa, the son of Vikartana, went with full force toward Arjuna seeking battle, as an elephant goes toward a rival elephant for the sake of a cow in rut.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ yayau śalyo madrāṇām īśvaro balī duryodhanādayas tv anye brāhmaṇaiḥ saha saṃgatāḥ mṛdupūrvam ayatnena pratyayudhyaṃs tadāhave
english: The mighty Śalya, lord of the Madras, went against Bhīmasena, while Duryodhana and the others, in conflict with the brahmins, fought gently and without effort in that battle.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ pratyavidhyad āpatantaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ dhīmān vikṛṣya balavad dhanuḥ
english: Then wise Arjuna, drawing his bow with full strength, shot back at the onrushing Karṇa, son of Vikartana, with three arrows.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śarāṇāṃ vegena śitānāṃ tigmatejasām vimuhyamāno rādheyo yatnāt tam anudhāvati
english: Stunned by the force of those sharp arrows blazing with fierce energy, Rādheya strove with all effort and pressed after him.

sanskrit: tāv ubhāv apy anirdeśyau lāghavāj jayatāṃ varau ayudhyetāṃ susaṃrabdhāv anyonyavijayaiṣiṇau
english: Both of them, incomparable in swiftness, foremost among conquerors, fought with fierce intensity, each striving for victory over the other.

sanskrit: kṛte pratikṛtaṃ paśya paśya bāhubalaṃ ca me iti śūrārthavacanair ābhāṣetāṃ parasparam
english: "See stroke met with counterstroke — see the might of my arms!" — with such warrior-proud words they addressed each other in turn.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunasya bhujayor vīryam apratimaṃ bhuvi jñātvā vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ saṃrabdhaḥ samayodhayat
english: Then Karṇa the son of Vikartana, recognizing the incomparable valor of Arjuna's arms, fought on enraged, matching him blow for blow.

sanskrit: arjunena prayuktāṃs tān bāṇān vegavatas tadā pratihatya nanādoccaiḥ sainyās tam abhipūjayan
english: Deflecting those swift arrows launched by Arjuna, Karṇa then roared aloud, and the soldiers honored him with acclaim.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca tuṣyāmi te vipramukhya bhujavīryasya saṃyuge aviṣādasya caivāsya śastrāstravinayasya ca
english: Karṇa said: "I am pleased with you, O foremost of brahmins, with the strength of your arms in combat, with your undaunted spirit, and with your mastery of both weapons and missile-lore."

sanskrit: kiṃ tvaṃ sākṣād dhanurvedo rāmo vā viprasattama atha sākṣād dharihayaḥ sākṣād vā viṣṇur acyutaḥ
english: "Are you Dhanurveda incarnate, or Rāma himself, O best of brahmins? Or are you perhaps Indra of the bay horses in person, or Viṣṇu the Infallible in bodily form?"

sanskrit: ātmapracchādanārthaṃ vai bāhuvīryam upāśritaḥ viprarūpaṃ vidhāyedaṃ tato māṃ pratiyudhyase
english: "Concealing your true identity and relying on the strength of your arms, you have assumed this brahmin form and then fight me."

sanskrit: na hi mām āhave kruddham anyaḥ sākṣāc chacīpateḥ pumān yodhayituṃ śaktaḥ pāṇḍavād vā kirīṭinaḥ
english: "No man other than the lord of Śacī himself or the diademed Pāṇḍava would be capable of fighting me in battle when I am enraged."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam evaṃvādinaṃ tatra phalgunaḥ pratyabhāṣata nāsmi karṇa dhanurvedo nāsmi rāmaḥ pratāpavān brāhmaṇo 'smi yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To Karṇa speaking thus, Phalguna replied there: "I am not Dhanurveda, O Karṇa, nor am I the glorious Rāma. I am a brahmin, the foremost in battle, the best among all who bear weapons."

sanskrit: brāhme pauraṃdare cāstre niṣṭhito guruśāsanāt sthito 'smy adya raṇe jetuṃ tvāṃ vīrāvicalo bhava
english: "I am accomplished in both the Brahmā and Pauramdara weapon-sciences by the teaching of my guru. I stand here today in battle to conquer you. Stand firm, O hero."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rādheyo yuddhāt karṇo nyavartata brahmaṃ tejas tadājayyaḥ manyamāno mahārathaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Rādheya Karṇa withdrew from the battle, that great chariot-warrior deeming the brahminic energy arrayed against him unconquerable.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ tūpeyatus tatra rājañ śalyavṛkodarau balinau yugapan mattau spardhayā ca balena ca
english: O king, Śalya and Vṛkodara, both mighty, intoxicated with pride and strength, engaged in combat simultaneously, rival in their rivalry.

sanskrit: anyonyam āhvayantau tau mattāv iva mahāgajau muṣṭibhir jānubhiś caiva nighnantāv itaretaram muhūrtaṃ tau tathānyonyaṃ samare paryakarṣatām
english: Challenging each other like two great maddened elephants, they struck one another with fists and with knees, and for a moment they dragged each other about on the battlefield.

sanskrit: tato bhīmaḥ samutkṣipya bāhubhyāṃ śalyam āhave nyavadhīd balināṃ śreṣṭho jahasur brāhmaṇās tataḥ
english: Then Bhīma, foremost among the strong, lifted Śalya with both arms in the midst of battle and hurled him down; thereupon the brahmins laughed.

sanskrit: tatrāścaryaṃ bhīmasenaś cakāra puruṣarṣabhaḥ yac chalyaṃ patitaṃ bhūmau nāhanad balinaṃ balī
english: There the bull among men, Bhīmasena, performed a wonder — though mighty himself, he did not strike the mighty Śalya as he lay fallen on the ground.

sanskrit: pātite bhīmasenena śalye karṇe ca śaṅkite śaṅkitāḥ sarvarājānaḥ parivavrur vṛkodaram
english: With Śalya thrown down by Bhīmasena and Karṇa intimidated, all the frightened kings surrounded Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: ūcuś ca sahitās tatra sādhv ime brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ vijñāyantāṃ kvajanmānaḥ kvanivāsās tathaiva ca
english: And they said to one another: "These are certainly foremost among brahmins. Let it be known where they were born and where they dwell."

sanskrit: ko hi rādhāsutaṃ karmaṃ śakto yodhayituṃ raṇe anyatra rāmād droṇād vā kṛpād vāpi śaradvataḥ
english: "Who indeed would be capable of fighting Rādhā's son in battle other than Rāma, or Droṇa, or Kṛpa son of Śaradvat,

sanskrit: kṛṣṇād vā devakīputrāt phalgunād vā paraṃtapāt ko vā duryodhanaṃ śaktaḥ pratiyodhayituṃ raṇe
english: or Kṛṣṇa the son of Devakī, or Phalguna the scorcher of foes? And who would be capable of fighting back against Duryodhana in battle,

sanskrit: tathaiva madrarājānaṃ śalyaṃ balavatāṃ varam baladevād ṛte vīrāt pāṇḍavād vā vṛkodarāt
english: and likewise against Śalya the king of the Madras, best among the strong — no one but Baladeva the hero, or the Pāṇḍava Vṛkodara?"

sanskrit: kriyatām avahāro 'smād yuddhād brāhmaṇasaṃyutāt athainān upalabhyeha punar yotsyāmahe vayam
english: "Let withdrawal be made from this battle combined with brahmins; then, once we have identified them here, we shall fight them again."

sanskrit: tat karma bhīmasya samīkṣya kṛṣṇaḥ; kuntīsutau tau pariśaṅkamānaḥ nivārayām āsa mahīpatīṃs tān; dharmeṇa labdhety anunīya sarvān
english: Kṛṣṇa, observing that feat of Bhīma and growing suspicious about those two sons of Kuntī, restrained those kings, appeasing them all with the argument that she had been lawfully won.

sanskrit: ta evaṃ saṃnivṛttās tu yuddhād yuddhaviśāradāḥ yathāvāsaṃ yayuḥ sarve vismitā rājasattamāḥ
english: Those foremost of kings, skilled in battle, having thus been turned back from the fight, all departed to their own lodgings in amazement.

sanskrit: vṛtto brahmottaro raṅgaḥ pāñcālī brāhmaṇair vṛtā iti bruvantaḥ prayayur ye tatrāsan samāgatāḥ
english: "The arena has been dominated by a brahmin; the Pāñcālī princess has been chosen by brahmins" — saying this, all who had assembled there departed.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇais tu praticchannau rauravājinavāsibhiḥ kṛcchreṇa jagmatus tatra bhīmasenadhanaṃjayau
english: Bhīmasena and Dhanañjaya, covered with disguise by brahmins wearing robes of black-deer hide, with difficulty made their way back.

sanskrit: vimuktau janasaṃbādhāc chatrubhiḥ parivikṣatau kṛṣṇayānugatau tatra nṛvīrau tau virejatuḥ
english: Free from the press of the crowd, scratched by enemies, followed by Kṛṣṇa, those two heroes among men shone brilliantly there.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ mātā bahuvidhaṃ vināśaṃ paryacintayat anāgacchatsu putreṣu bhaikṣakāle 'tigacchati
english: Their mother anxiously thought of many forms of destruction as the appointed hour for alms-gathering passed by and her sons had not yet returned.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrair hatā na syur vijñāya kurupuṃgavāḥ māyānvitair vā rakṣobhiḥ sughorair dṛḍhavairibhiḥ
english: "Might the bulls of the Kurus have been slain by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, knowing who they are, or by Rākṣasas endowed with illusion, those greatly terrifying and implacable foes?"

sanskrit: viparītaṃ mataṃ jātaṃ vyāsasyāpi mahātmanaḥ ity evaṃ cintayām āsa sutasnehānvitā pṛthā
english: "Has even the prediction of the great-souled Vyāsa turned out contrary?" — thus Pṛthā meditated, filled with maternal love for her sons.

sanskrit: mahaty athāparāhṇe tu ghanaiḥ sūrya ivāvṛtaḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ prāviśat tatra jiṣṇur brahmapuraskṛtaḥ
english: Then in the late afternoon, Jiṣṇu entered there, surrounded by brahmins, like the sun veiled by clouds, with brahmins preceding him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gatvā tu tāṃ bhārgavakarmaśālāṃ; pārthau pṛthāṃ prāpya mahānubhāvau tāṃ yājñasenīṃ paramapratītau; bhikṣety athāvedayatāṃ narāgryau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Going to that workshop of the Bhārgava smith, the two Pārthas of great majesty reached Pṛthā and joyfully announced to that daughter of Yajña-sena and those foremost of men: "We have received alms."

sanskrit: kuṭīgatā sā tv anavekṣya putrān; uvāca bhuṅkteti sametya sarve paścāt tu kuntī prasamīkṣya kanyāṃ; kaṣṭaṃ mayā bhāṣitam ity uvāca
english: She, having entered the hut without looking at her sons, said "Share it equally among you all." But afterwards Kuntī, looking closely at the maiden, said: "Alas, what a thing I have said!"

sanskrit: sādharmabhītā hi vilajjamānā; tāṃ yājñasenīṃ paramapratītām pāṇau gṛhītvopajagāma kuntī; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ vākyam uvāca cedam
english: Afraid of unrighteousness and ashamed, Kuntī took that greatly noble daughter of Yajñasena by the hand, approached Yudhiṣṭhira, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: iyaṃ hi kanyā drupadasya rājñas; tavānujābhyāṃ mayi saṃnisṛṣṭā yathocitaṃ putra mayāpi coktaṃ; sametya bhuṅkteti nṛpa pramādāt
english: "This maiden is the daughter of King Drupada, entrusted to me by your younger brothers, O son. Through inadvertence I too spoke the fitting word, O king: 'Share it equally among you all.'"

sanskrit: kathaṃ mayā nānṛtam uktam adya; bhavet kurūṇām ṛṣabha bravīhi pāñcālarājasya sutām adharmo; na copavarteta nabhūtapūrvaḥ
english: "How can what I said today not become a falsehood, O bull of the Kurus? Tell me. Yet neither should unrighteousness befall the daughter of the Pāñcāla king — something unprecedented."

sanskrit: muhūrtamātraṃ tv anucintya rājā; yudhiṣṭhiro mātaram uttamaujāḥ kuntīṃ samāśvāsya kurupravīro; dhanaṃjayaṃ vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira of highest valor, the foremost of the Kurus, having pondered for a moment, reassured his mother Kuntī and spoke these words to Dhanañjaya:

sanskrit: tvayā jitā pāṇḍava yājñasenī; tvayā ca toṣiṣyati rājaputrī prajvālyatāṃ hūyatāṃ cāpi vahnir; gṛhāṇa pāṇiṃ vidhivat tvam asyāḥ
english: "By you, O Pāṇḍava, was Yājñasenī won; by you will this princess be pleased. Let fire be kindled and the oblation poured — take her hand in accordance with the rites."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca mā māṃ narendra tvam adharmabhājaṃ; kṛthā na dharmo hy ayam īpsito 'nyaiḥ bhavān niveśyaḥ prathamaṃ tato 'yaṃ; bhīmo mahābāhur acintyakarmā
english: Arjuna said: "Do not make me, O king of men, a partaker in unrighteousness; this is not the dharma desired by others. You should be wedded first, then this long-armed Bhīma of inconceivable deeds,

sanskrit: ahaṃ tato nakulo 'nantaraṃ me; mādrīsutaḥ sahadevo jaghanyaḥ vṛkodaro 'haṃ ca yamau ca rājann; iyaṃ ca kanyā bhavataḥ sma sarve
english: then I, then Nakula next to me, then Mādrī's son Sahadeva the youngest. O king, Vṛkodara, I, and the twins — this maiden and all of us are yours to command."

sanskrit: evaṃgate yat karaṇīyam atra; dharmyaṃ yaśasyaṃ kuru tat pracintya pāñcālarājasya ca yat priyaṃ syāt; tad brūhi sarve sma vaśe sthitās te
english: "Given this situation, reflect on what is to be done here that is righteous and honorable, and what would please the Pāñcāla king. Speak — we all stand ready at your command."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te dṛṣṭvā tatra tiṣṭhantīṃ sarve kṛṣṇāṃ yaśasvinīm saṃprekṣyānyonyam āsīnā hṛdayais tām adhārayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: All of them, seeing the glorious Kṛṣṇa standing there, looked at one another as they sat and held her in their hearts.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ hi draupadīṃ dṛṣṭvā sarveṣām amitaujasām saṃpramathyendriyagrāmaṃ prādurāsīn manobhavaḥ
english: For all of them of boundless valor, upon seeing Draupadī, desire arose, churning through all their senses.

sanskrit: kāmyaṃ rūpaṃ hi pāñcālyā vidhātrā vihitaṃ svayam babhūvādhikam anyābhyaḥ sarvabhūtamanoharam
english: For the Pāñcālī's lovely form had been fashioned by the Creator himself, surpassing all other women, captivating the hearts of all beings.

sanskrit: teṣām ākārabhāvajñaḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dvaipāyanavacaḥ kṛtsnaṃ saṃsmaran vai nararṣabha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī and knower of their outward signs and inner states, fully recalling the words of Dvaipāyana, O bull among men,

sanskrit: abravīt sa hi tān bhrātṝn mithobhedabhayān nṛpaḥ sarveṣāṃ draupadī bhāryā bhaviṣyati hi naḥ śubhā
english: that king, fearing discord among them, spoke to his brothers: "The auspicious Draupadī shall be the wife of all of us."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhrātur vacas tat prasamīkṣya sarve; jyeṣṭhasya pāṇḍos tanayās tadānīm tam evārthaṃ dhyāyamānā manobhir; āsāṃ cakrur atha tatrāmitaujāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: All the sons of Pāṇḍu, having considered those words of their eldest brother, then of boundless energy, held that very matter in their minds and sat there.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇipravīras tu kurupravīrān; āśaṅkamānaḥ saharauhiṇeyaḥ jagāma tāṃ bhārgavakarmaśālāṃ; yatrāsate te puruṣapravīrāḥ
english: But the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis, together with the son of Rohiṇī, being apprehensive about the foremost of the Kurus, went to that workshop of the Bhārgava smith where those foremost of men were sitting.

sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭaṃ pṛthudīrghabāhuṃ; dadarśa kṛṣṇaḥ saharauhiṇeyaḥ ajātaśatruṃ parivārya tāṃś ca; upopaviṣṭāñ jvalanaprakāśān
english: There Kṛṣṇa together with the son of Rohiṇī saw the long and broad-armed Ajātaśatru seated, with those others surrounding him, seated nearby, blazing like fires.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd vāsudevo 'bhigamya; kuntīsutaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham kṛṣṇo 'ham asmīti nipīḍya pādau; yudhiṣṭhirasyājamīḍhasya rājñaḥ
english: Then Vāsudeva approached and, pressing the feet of the best among upholders of dharma, said: "I am Kṛṣṇa" — the feet of King Yudhiṣṭhira of the Ajamidha lineage.

sanskrit: tathaiva tasyāpy anu rauhiṇeyas; tau cāpi hṛṣṭāḥ kuravo 'bhyanandan pitṛṣvasuś cāpi yadupravīrāv; agṛhṇatāṃ bhāratamukhya pādau
english: Likewise the son of Rohiṇī did the same after him; and the Kurus rejoiced and welcomed them. Also the foremost of the Yadus grasped the feet of their father's sister, O chief of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: ajātaśatruś ca kurupravīraḥ; papraccha kṛṣṇaṃ kuśalaṃ nivedya kathaṃ vayaṃ vāsudeva tvayeha; gūḍhā vasanto viditāḥ sma sarve
english: And Ajātaśatru, the foremost of the Kurus, after reporting his own welfare, asked Kṛṣṇa: "How, O Vāsudeva, were all of us known to you while we were living here in disguise?"

sanskrit: tam abravīd vāsudevaḥ prahasya; gūḍho 'py agnir jñāyata eva rājan taṃ vikramaṃ pāṇḍaveyānatītya; ko 'nyaḥ kartā vidyate mānuṣeṣu
english: Vāsudeva replied with a smile: "Even hidden fire is perceived, O king. Who else among men is to be found who could perform that feat which surpasses the Pāṇḍavas?"

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tasmāt pāvakāt saṃpramuktā; yūyaṃ sarve pāṇḍavāḥ śatrusāhāḥ diṣṭyā pāpo dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraḥ; sahāmātyo na sakāmo 'bhaviṣyat
english: "By good fortune all of you Pāṇḍavas, conquerors of enemies, have been freed from that fire. By good fortune the wicked son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra along with his minister has not had his desire fulfilled."

sanskrit: bhadraṃ vo 'stu nihitaṃ yad guhāyāṃ; vivardhadhvaṃ jvalana ivedhyamānaḥ mā vo vidyuḥ pārthivāḥ ke caneha; yāsyāvahe śibirāyaiva tāvat so 'nujñātaḥ pāṇḍavenāvyayaśrīḥ; prāyāc chīghraṃ baladevena sārdham
english: "May what is hidden in the cave be auspicious for you. Grow strong like a fire being kindled. Let no kings here discover you." Having thus been granted leave by the Pāṇḍava, Kṛṣṇa of undying glory swiftly departed together with Baladeva toward the camp.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu pāñcālyaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ kurunandanau anvagacchat tadā yāntau bhārgavasya niveśanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Dhṛṣṭadyumna the Pāñcāla prince followed behind those two delights of the Kurus as they went to the dwelling of the Bhārgava.

sanskrit: so 'jñāyamānaḥ puruṣān avadhāya samantataḥ svayam ārān niviṣṭo 'bhūd bhārgavasya niveśane
english: He, remaining unrecognized, posted men all around and himself settled at a distance within the Bhārgava's dwelling.

sanskrit: sāye 'tha bhīmas tu ripupramāthī; jiṣṇur yamau cāpi mahānubhāvau bhaikṣaṃ caritvā tu yudhiṣṭhirāya; nivedayāṃ cakrur adīnasattvāḥ
english: Then in the evening, Bhīma the crusher of enemies, Jiṣṇu, and the twins of great majesty, those of undaunted spirit, having gathered alms, presented them to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tatas tu kuntī drupadātmajāṃ tām; uvāca kāle vacanaṃ vadānyā ato 'gram ādāya kuruṣva bhadre; baliṃ ca viprāya ca dehi bhikṣām
english: Then Kuntī the bountiful spoke in proper time to that daughter of Drupada: "Take of it first, dear girl, set aside an offering, and give alms to the brahmin."

sanskrit: ye cānnam icchanti dadasva tebhyaḥ; pariśritā ye parito manuṣyāḥ tataś ca śeṣaṃ pravibhajya śīghram; ardhaṃ caturṇāṃ mama cātmanaś ca
english: "To those who desire food, give to them — the people who have gathered all around. Then, having divided the remainder swiftly, give half for the four and for myself."

sanskrit: ardhaṃ ca bhīmāya dadāhi bhadre; ya eṣa mattarṣabhatulyarūpaḥ śyāmo yuvā saṃhananopapanna; eṣo hi vīro bahubhuk sadaiva
english: "And give the other half to Bhīma, dear girl — he who resembles a bull in rut, that dark young man of powerful frame; for this hero is always a great eater."

sanskrit: sā hṛṣṭarūpaiva tu rājaputrī; tasyā vacaḥ sādhv aviśaṅkamānā yathāvad uktaṃ pracakāra sādhvī; te cāpi sarve 'bhyavajahrur annam
english: That princess, her face filled with joy, accepting her words without hesitation as right and proper, the virtuous one carried out exactly as instructed; and all of them partook of the food.
